content.title: About
content.content: Popcorn is a type of dried corn kernel that expands and puffs up when heated, creating a light, airy snack. Plain popcorn has a neutral flavor, crunchy texture, and low fat content. It is commonly enjoyed at movies, sporting events, and at home.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Popcorn is the only variety of corn that can "pop" due to its high internal moisture.
The first commercial popcorn appeared in the United States in the late 19th century.
In the 1940s popcorn became a staple in movie theaters when it started being sold from vending machines.
There are more than 30 popcorn varieties, differing in size, shape, and flavor.
Popcorn can be prepared in a microwave, on the stovetop, in an air popper, or in a dedicated popcorn maker.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: Air‑popped popcorn without butter or sugar contains about 380 kcal per 100 g, making it a lighter snack compared with many other processed foods.

items.title: Rich in fiber
items.content: The dietary fiber in popcorn supports digestion and helps you feel full longer.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Popcorn provides polyphenols, which help combat oxidative stress.

items.title: Gluten‑free
items.content: Naturally free of gluten, popcorn is suitable for people with celiac disease.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Popcorn contains thiamine, niacin, and vitamin B6, important for metabolism.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Popcorn can raise blood sugar quickly, so individuals with diabetes should monitor portion sizes.

items.title: Added salt and oil
items.content: Large amounts of salt or oil increase calorie density and may negatively affect blood pressure.

items.title: Choking hazard
items.content: Small pieces can pose a choking risk for young children.

items.title: Corn allergy
items.content: A small number of people may be allergic to corn products, including popcorn.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Popcorn can be enjoyed plain or seasoned with salt, spices, cheese powder, or caramel. It is often mixed with nuts, dried fruit, or chocolate. For a healthier option, pop it without oil in a microwave or on a dry pan.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store popcorn in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. For longer shelf life keep it in the refrigerator to prevent the oils from going rancid. Discard popcorn that becomes soft, moist, or develops an off‑odor.
